title: Pete Buttigieg endorses Jonathan Nez for Arizona's 2nd Congressional District
text:
June 1, former U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg announced his endorsement of Jonathan Nez for Arizona’s Second Congressional District. Buttigieg cited Nez’s leadership on rural infrastructure, tribal communities, and economic development as key reasons for his support.
“President Nez is a proven leader who brings people together to deliver real results,” Buttigieg said. “During my time leading the U.S. Department of Transportation, I worked with him to improve infrastructure for Arizona’s tribal communities and rural areas. He knows how to advocate for better roads, water infrastructure, broadband, and economic opportunity in places too often overlooked by Washington. Arizona needs and deserves his leadership in Congress,” according to Buttigieg.
As President of the Navajo Nation, Nez worked with Buttigieg and the federal government to secure investments in roads, bridges, broadband, and transportation infrastructure throughout tribal and rural communities. Nez responded to the endorsement, saying, “I’m very grateful to have Secretary Buttigieg’s support. Sec. Pete believes, as I do, that Americans are tired of partisan games and deserve real results to lower costs and build a future where all Americans can succeed. We worked together to push for infrastructure investments that created jobs, improved public safety, and strengthened rural and tribal communities. In Congress, I’ll continue fighting to make sure rural Arizona families aren’t left behind,” according to Nez.
The endorsement comes as Nez’s campaign continues to build momentum, focusing on affordability, infrastructure, water security, and restoring trust in government. Nez is the 2024 Democratic nominee for Congress in Arizona’s 2nd District. He grew up in rural Arizona and began his public service career in Shonto on the Navajo Nation before being elected President of the Navajo Nation in 2018.
Nez’s campaign states that he is running to lower costs for families, deliver water security to all Arizonans, and give rural Arizonans a voice in Congress. He lives in Flagstaff with his wife, Phefelia, and their two sons. More information about the campaign can be found on the official website, according to Jonathan Nez for Congress .
